text: Sex is not love. Going out with someone is not love. Talking to someone 24 hours a day, seven days a week is not love. Staying up all night for someone is not love. Love is when someone sees the parts of you that you try to hide, the fears, the anger, the exhaustion, and still chooses to stay. It is when someone offers you emotional safety, when your mind is at war with itself. It is when someone becomes your calm in the middle of the chaos, your anchor in the storm. Love is someone who talks to you when you are overwhelmed, reminding you of your worth when you cannot remember it yourself. Love is standing beside you while you heal without trying to fix you. It is when someone understands the silence behind you, I am fine, and offers the comfort you do not always know how to ask for. Love is loyalty that does not need validation, faithfulness that stays strong even when you are apart. It is someone who protects your vulnerabilities, makes joy feel like healing, and still chooses you when your heart longs to love. True love is constant, patient, and safe. But there is something you need to understand. Before anyone can give you that kind of love, you have to learn how to give it to yourself. And that is the hardest part, because nobody teaches you how to take care of yourself from the inside, how to calm your own mind, how to be your own anchor when there is no one else. Share this with that special person. Write in the comments, love is care, if this made sense to you. And if you want to learn how to build that kind of peace within yourself, how to stop depending on someone else to feel whole, how to become your own calm before asking anyone else to be it for you. I spent over 20 years learning in silence how to do exactly that. And everything I know is inside the way back to stillness. The link is in my profile.
